title: Windows Server: Event IDs You Must Know

scenes.line1: Can you explain a server reboot?
scenes.line2: Which event IDs tell the story?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why a Windows server rebooted? Which event IDs reveal the cause?
These event IDs come up all the time. Logon attempts, account lockouts, planned restarts, and unexpected shutdowns—each has its own code.

scenes.title: Check planned restarts
scenes.say: To see who or what triggered a planned restart, filter for event ID ten seventy-four in the system log.
Planned restarts have event ID ten seventy-four. If you see six thousand eight or forty-one, the server crashed or lost power.

scenes.question: Does 1074 mean a crash?
scenes.right: No, 1074 means someone or something requested a restart. Crashes show up as six thousand eight or forty-one.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: does event ID ten seventy-four mean the server crashed? Not at all. It means a restart was requested. Crashes use different IDs.
